items.title: Pulmonary Vein Reconnection Burden and Extra-Pulmonary Vein Ablation During Second Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation in the Pre-Pulsed-Field Ablation Era: A Multicenter Registry.
items.abstract: Contemporary procedural characteristics of second catheter ablation (CA) for atrial fibrillation (AF) remain incompletely characterized. To investigate procedural characteristics and clinical implications of pulmonary vein (PV) reconnection during second CA for AF. We analyzed 854 patients who underwent second CA for AF between April 2021 and March 2024 at nine institutions before the clinical adoption of pulsed-field ablation. Patients were stratified according to the number of reconnected PVs identified during the procedures: none (0), single (1), and multiple (≥ 2). The primary endpoint was freedom from atrial arrhythmia recurrence, assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. During second CA, PV reconnections (21% per vein) were identified and re-isolated in all affected PVs. Patients with no PV reconnection accounted for 55.5% (n = 474) of the cohort and underwent extra-PV ablation more frequently than those with single (n = 146) or multiple (n = 234) reconnected PVs. During a median follow-up of 706 days, multiple reconnected PVs with subsequent re-isolation were associated with a lower risk of atrial arrhythmia recurrence than no PV reconnection. This association remained significant after multivariable adjustment (hazard ratio 0.69, 95% confidence interval 0.50-0.95; p = 0.023) and was more pronounced in patients without symptomatic heart failure (p for interaction = 0.009). Enlarged left atrial diameter, non-paroxysmal AF, and symptomatic heart failure were also independently associated with recurrence, whereas additional extra-PV ablation was not. Re-isolation of multiple reconnected PVs was independently associated with a lower risk of atrial arrhythmia recurrence after second CA for AF, particularly in patients without symptomatic heart failure.

items.title: Finerenone in Patients with Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis.
items.abstract: Mineralocorticoid receptor overactivation is implicated in podocyte injury and glomerulosclerosis. In a prespecified analysis of the FIND-CKD trial, we examined the efficacy and safety of finerenone in participants with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS). The FIND-CKD trial randomized 1584 adults with nondiabetic CKD (eGFR ≥25 to <60 ml/min/1.73 m2 and urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio [UACR] ≥200 to <500 mg/g, or eGFR ≥25 to <90 ml/min/1.73 m2 and UACR ≥500 to ≤3500 mg/g) on stable renin-angiotensin system inhibition, 1:1 to finerenone (10 or 20 mg) or placebo. Reported outcomes include total eGFR slope (baseline to month 32; FIND-CKD primary outcome), a kidney composite (sustained ≥57% eGFR decline from baseline or kidney failure; FIND-CKD secondary outcome), changes in urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR; exploratory outcome), and adverse events (safety outcome). Among the 215 participants with FSGS, mean (SD) baseline eGFR was 45 (17) ml/min/1.73 m2, and median (Q1, Q3) UPCR was 1427 (947, 2120) mg/g; 50% each had primary (n=108) and secondary (n=107) FSGS. Finerenone reduced the total eGFR slope versus placeboby 1.3 ml/min/1.73 m2/year (95% CI, 0.5-2.2; P=0.002). This effect was consistent among the 167 (78%) participants with a biopsy-proven FSGS diagnosis (1.4 ml/min/1.73 m2/year), and among participants with primary or secondary FSGS (P-interaction 0.84). Finerenone yielded a hazard ratio of 0.58 (95% CI, 0.30-1.15) versus placebo for the kidney composite outcome. From baseline to month 12, finerenone lowered UPCR by 41% (95% CI, 26%-53%) versus placebo and increased the likelihood of achieving UPCR <700 mg/g (odds ratio at month 12: 6.8 [95% CI, 3.0-17.2]). A post hoc exploratory proteomics analysis showed that finerenone versus placebo reduced markers of fibrosis, inflammation, and components of the filtration barrier. Hyperkalemia-related adverse events occurred in 15 (15%) and 23 (20%) participants assigned to finerenone or placebo, respectively. Finerenone was well-tolerated and preserved kidney function, lowered proteinuria, and reduced markers of fibrosis, inflammation, and components of filtration barrier in FIND-CKD participants with FSGS.

items.title: Exercise and insulin independently stimulate galactose uptake into human skeletal muscle.
items.abstract: Carbohydrate choice affects glycaemic responses during and after exercise, particularly for individuals with impaired glucose regulation. Galactose causes smaller glycaemic excursions than glucose but is thought to require hepatic conversion to glucose via the Leloir pathway before peripheral use. Whether galactose is directly taken up by skeletal muscle, and whether this is regulated by exercise and insulin remains unclear. In this randomised, controlled crossover trial, eight healthy men (age 68 ± 4 years; body mass index 24.7 ± 2.1 kg/m 2 ) completed two 4 h study days, with and without a hyperinsulinaemic-euglycaemic clamp (1.0 mU/kg/min). Galactose turnover was assessed using a primed-constant galactose infusion. Participants performed one-legged, high-intensity knee-extension exercise at maximal capacity, with the contralateral leg as a non-exercised control. Skeletal muscle galactose uptake was quantified by dynamic [ 1 8 F]FDGal positron emission tomography (PET), and arteriovenous (AV) exchange across the leg was determined from femoral blood samples combined with [ 1 5 O]H 2 O PET-measured leg perfusion. Exercise and insulin markedly increased galactose uptake (exercise effect: P  1 8 F]fluoro-2-deoxygalactose in combination with a one-legged knee-extension ergometer, we demonstrated that human skeletal muscle can directly take up galactose. Both exercise and insulin markedly increased skeletal muscle galactose uptake, with an additive effect when combined. Exercise primarily increased galactose uptake by enhancing muscle blood flow, whereas insulin exerted its effect by promoting phosphorylation and intracellular trapping. Further studies are required to determine whether galactose is incorporated into skeletal muscle glycogen to a physiologically meaningful extent.

items.title: An Oscillometric Readout Assessing the Degree of Airway Smooth Muscle Activation In Vivo.
items.abstract: Oscillometry is a technique for probing respiratory mechanics that is emerging in clinical settings. One advantage of oscillometry that has yet to be fully exploited is its fine temporal resolution, which makes it suitable for capturing changes in lung mechanics that occur over short timescales, such as those caused by a deep inspiration (DI) or by airway smooth muscle. Herein, we hypothesized that the short-lived decrease in respiratory system resistance at 5 Hz (R rs5 ) induced by a DI is attributable to airway smooth muscle. We assessed, for the first time, the temporal response to DI following administration of the bronchodilator salbutamol to confirm that the DI-induced decrease in R rs5 is mediated by airway smooth muscle. Thirty-seven very mild-to-mild asthmatics underwent oscillometry before, during, and after a DI, both before and after the inhalation of salbutamol (200 µg). R rs5 pre-DI and during the first tidal breath post-DI was compared to quantify the DI response. R rs5 decreased by 12.7 ± 19.8% in response to DI, and this response was virtually abolished by salbutamol (p = 0.001). The DI response also correlated with the response to salbutamol (r = 0.47, p = 0.003). These results indicate that the temporary decrease in R rs5 caused by DI is attributable to airway smooth muscle. This change in R rs5 pre versus post-DI is readily measured, and its magnitude is likely to reflect the degree of airway smooth muscle activation. It holds the potential to aid in the diagnosis of asthma and in predicting responses to bronchodilator drugs.

items.title: Neutrophil-tropic APL@Mn 3 O 4 nanozymes alleviate myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury through redox regulation.
items.abstract: Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI) is driven by coupled oxidative and inflammatory amplification after reperfusion, with activated neutrophils acting as early upstream effectors that propagate secondary cardiomyocyte injury. Strategies limited to downstream oxidative damage may therefore be insufficient to interrupt this reinforcing cascade. We developed an agglutinated-protein liposome formulation encapsulating Mn 3 O 4 nanozymes (APL@Mn 3 O 4 ), designed to integrate delivery directed toward activated neutrophils with catalytic redox regulation. The agglutinated-protein liposomal surface supported complement-associated tropism toward activated neutrophils under inflammatory conditions, whereas the Mn 3 O 4 core retained catalytic antioxidant activity for reactive oxygen species (ROS) regulation. In vitro , APL@Mn 3 O 4 reduced neutrophil oxidative and inflammatory responses without measurably impairing migratory capacity under the tested conditions. In a neutrophil-cardiomyocyte co-culture system, APL@Mn 3 O 4 attenuated oxidative stress and apoptosis in injured cardiomyocytes. In vivo , APL@Mn 3 O 4 preferentially associated with circulating neutrophils, attenuated oxidative and inflammatory myocardial injury, and improved post-reperfusion cardiac remodeling and function. These findings support APL@Mn 3 O 4 as a neutrophil-tropic nanozyme platform for alleviating MIRI by attenuating pathological neutrophil-associated oxidative and inflammatory activity and reducing secondary cardiomyocyte injury.

items.title: Surveillance of adverse events following immunisation in Australia, 2024.
items.abstract: This report summarises Australia's spontaneous surveillance data for adverse events following immunisation (AEFI) for all vaccines administered in 2024, reported to the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA). An adverse event(s) following immunisation is defined as any untoward medical occurrence which follows immunisation but does not necessarily have a causal relationship with use of the vaccine. Analyses of AEFI data are done continuously and also annually to detect new potential safety issues or changes to known safety issues. Overall, there were 6,232 AEFI reports for vaccines administered in 2024. This represents an annual AEFI reporting rate of 22.9 per 100,000 population and 25.7 per 100,000 vaccine doses, compared with 20.8 per 100,000 population and 24.1 per 100,000 doses in 2023. The slight increase in the AEFI reporting rates observed in 2024 was likely driven by the introduction of a new recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV, Shingrix) which replaced the live attenuated zoster vaccine (ZLV, Zostavax) on the National Immunisation Program (NIP) from November 2023, along with the expansion of the eligible population for zoster vaccination. In 2024, RZV (Shingrix) was associated with the highest number of reported AEFIs. The most frequently reported adverse events following immunisation were medication errors; hypersensitivity; gastrointestinal nonspecific symptoms; pyrexia; and injection site reaction. Among vaccines newly introduced in 2024, the most commonly reported adverse events were medication errors and nonspecific gastrointestinal symptoms for COVID-19 vaccines (Comirnaty XBB.1.5 and Spikevax XBB.1.5); hypersensitivity and pyrexia for the DTPa-HepB-IPV-Hib vaccine (Vaxelis); medication errors and exposure during pregnancy for the adjuvanted recombinant respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) pre-fusion F protein vaccine (Arexvy); and hypersensitivity and nonspecific gastrointestinal symptoms for RZV (Shingrix). Fewer deaths were reported following vaccination in 2024 (28 reports) than in 2023 (34 reports). None of the 28 reported deaths in 2024 indicated an emerging safety signal.

items.title: Tumo​r-associated macrophages in ovarian, prostate, thyroid and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors: molecular crosstalk and therapeutic perspectives.
items.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are key regulators of the tumor microenvironment and play dual roles in endocrine cancer progression by exhibiting remarkable functional plasticity beyond the conventional M1/M2 paradigm. Their interactions with tumor cells influence immune evasion, angiogenesis, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance through complex signaling networks and extracellular vesicle-mediated communication. This review summarizes the current understanding of TAM biology across some key endocrine and hormone-dependent cancers, including ovarian, prostate, thyroid, and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, highlighting their prognostic significance and molecular mechanisms. We further discuss emerging TAM-targeted therapeutic strategies, including macrophage depletion, immune checkpoint modulation, macrophage reprogramming, and nanoparticle-based approaches. Finally, we outline the challenges associated with clinical translation and emphasize the potential of single-cell and multi-omics technologies to enable precision macrophage-targeted therapies for endocrine cancers, including a summary of recent developments in the field of precision mapping of TAMs.

items.title: Anoikis in Gastric Cancer: Mechanistic Insights Into Metastatic Survival and Therapeutic Targeting.
items.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, largely because many patients present with advanced or metastatic disease. Anoikis, a specialized form of detachment-induced apoptosis, is a critical safeguard that eliminates epithelial cells after loss of appropriate extracellular matrix (ECM) and cell-cell adhesion; therefore, its disruption allows malignant cells to survive outside their native niche and acquire metastatic competence. In GC, anoikis resistance is central to tumor progression and peritoneal dissemination, enabling detached tumor cells to survive anchorage loss, mechanical stress, metabolic adaptation, and immune pressure before colonization. This review synthesizes current evidence on how anoikis is initiated, executed, and evaded in GC. Mechanistically, anoikis initiation begins with disruption of integrin-ECM and cadherin-mediated adhesion, followed by focal adhesion remodeling, cytoskeletal reorganization, and suppression or rewiring of adhesion-dependent survival signaling. Anoikis execution converges on mitochondrial and death-receptor apoptotic pathways, including Bcl-2 family regulation, caspase-8/caspase-9 activation, and executioner caspase cleavage. In contrast, anoikis evasion is driven by interconnected survival hubs, including integrin/FAK/Src, PI3K-AKT, MEK-ERK, NF-κB, Wnt/β-catenin, YAP/TEAD, BDNF/TrkB, and protective autophagy. GC-specific mediators such as TCF7L2/PLAUR, MYH9/CTNNB1, ITGBL1/AKT/FBLN2, CAV1/epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)/ITGB1, GRP94/YAP-TEAD1, GDF15/autophagy, and TRIM69/PRKCD/BDNF further illustrate how detached GC cells acquire metastatic survival capacity. Translationally, these pathways provide a rationale for biomarker-guided therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring anoikis sensitivity or disabling compensatory survival programs. Targeting anoikis resistance may therefore complement existing chemotherapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy approaches, particularly in GC subtypes characterized by peritoneal dissemination, EMT, YAP/TEAD activation, or integrin/PI3K-AKT pathway dependence.

items.title: Koinetic: a graph-based distance as a new ecological metric for microbial community differential analysis.
items.abstract: Phylogeny-aware beta diversity measures are essential in microbiome research, yet widely used metrics such as UniFrac and its variants rely on independent branch-length contributions and do not satisfy the Euclidean property, leading to distortions in ordination and kernel-based tests. These limitations underscore the need for a distance that is both phylogenetically coherent and geometrically valid. We introduce the Koinos Kinetic Distance (Koinetic), a phylogeny-aware dissimilarity that views microbial communities as interconnected assemblies rather than isolated taxa. "Koinos" emphasizes collective evaluation, while "kinetic" reflects how differences propagate dynamically across ecological networks and phylogenetic lineages. Koinetic leverages a graph Laplacian-based kernel to weight community differences by shared phylogeny, capturing ecological connectivity and clade relatedness. This design ensures Euclidean validity and enables seamless integration with kernel-based methods as well as geometry-preserving ordination. Controlled simulations and analyses of eight microbiome datasets spanning diverse body sites, disease contexts, and microbial profiling modalities demonstrate Koinetic's broad applicability. Compared with classical and phylogenetic metrics, including weighted, unweighted, and generalized UniFrac, unweighted Koinetic can improve power for phylogenetically localized prevalence shifts in the simulated settings, while weighted Koinetic performs comparably with weighted and generalized UniFrac under abundance-driven signals. Koinetic also shows strong performance in PERMANOVA and MiRKAT analyses assessing associations between microbial community composition and host phenotypes. Koinetic thus provides a general foundation for phylogeny-aware analysis, with a consistent geometric basis for visualization and statistical inference.

items.title: [Screening, diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up of hepatitis C virus-related liver disease].
items.abstract: Hepatitis C viral (HCV) infection has become curable. Eradication of the virus is essential from individual as well as from social aspects. Treatment in Hungary is based on a national consensus guideline, updated six-monthly. If there is no contraindication, demonstration of viral replication is the indication of therapy. Only direct-acting antiviral therapies are to be applied. At the time of publication of this guideline, only pan-genotypic combinations are available in Hungary. Based on fibrosis stage and on other (clinical, epidemiological, occupational, etc.) factors, a treatment prioritization system is available - however, all diagnosed infected individuals have access to reimbursed therapy nowadays. All infected individuals should be diagnosed and treated in a timely manner. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(46): 1847-1861. A hepatitis C-vírus (HCV)-fertőzés napjainkra gyógyíthatóvá vált. A fertőzöttség megszüntetése egyéni és társadalmi szempontból egyaránt előnyös és szükséges. A kezelés hazánkban a rendelkezésre álló gyógyszereken és finanszírozási lehetőségeken alapuló, félévenként megújított konszenzusajánlás szerint történik. Ellenjavallat hiányában a kezelés indikációja a vírusszaporodás kimutatása. A kezelés a HCV elleni direkt antivirális kombinációk valamelyikével végzendő. Az ajánlás közzétételének idejében hazánkban kizárólag a valamennyi genotípus esetében hatékony (pángenotípus) kombinált készítmények állnak rendelkezésre. A kezelésbe vonás sorrendjének meghatározására a fibrosis stádiumán és egyéb (klinikai, epidemiológiai, foglalkozás-egészségügyi stb.) szempontokon alapuló prioritási pontrendszer áll rendelkezésre – de napjainkban minden diagnosztizált beteg számára közfinanszírozott készítmények érhetők el. Valamennyi fertőzött mielőbbi kivizsgálása és kezelésbe vonása indokolt. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(46): 1847–1861.

items.title: Crocatin A: Neolignan From Piper crocatum Leaves Exhibited Promising Potency Against Hepatitis C Virus.
items.abstract: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) is a human pathogenic virus that infects approximately 50 million people worldwide. Current therapies are costly and may lead to drug resistance during prolonged treatment, highlighting the need for new antiviral agents. Piper crocatum has previously been reported to have anti-HCV activity. Accordingly, this study was aimed at isolating an active compound with anti-HCV activity and low cytotoxicity from the 70% ethanol extract of Piper crocatum. Isolation was performed using a bioassay-guided approach. Anti-HCV activity was evaluated in Huh7it-1 hepatocyte cells infected with the JFH1 strain. Structural elucidation of the isolated compound was carried out using 1 H and 13 C NMR spectroscopic analyses and comparison with published data. Bioassay-guided isolation of the 70% ethanol extract of Piper crocatum leaves resulted in the isolation of crocatin A, a neolignan compound with anti-HCV activity. The extract and crocatin A exhibited IC 50 values of 2.29 ± 0.19 and 1.90 ± 0.51  μg/mL, respectively. Both also had CC 50 values > 100 μg/mL against Huh7it-1 hepatocytes and the Vero cell line, indicating SI > 43.67 and > 52.63, respectively. Based on these findings, the extract and crocatin A possess anti-HCV activity while exhibiting no significant cytotoxicity toward the cell cultures used. The mode of action demonstrated stronger inhibition in the postentry step. Moreover, molecular docking was performed to predict the possible mechanism of action of the active compound, suggesting that crocatin A may interact favorably with the NS5B polymerase, potentially contributing to viral replication inhibition.

items.title: Development of Polyclonal Anti-HBsAg IgY Antibodies and Comparative Evaluation of Glutaraldehyde Versus Periodate HRP Bioconjugation for Hepatitis B Diagnosis.
items.abstract: Hepatitis B virus remains a major global health burden, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa, where affordable, specific and locally producible diagnostic tools are urgently needed. Conventional mammalian antibody-based assays can suffer from high background signals and interference in human sera. We developed a polyclonal chicken IgY reagent against the immunodominant "a" determinant of HBsAg, using consensus peptides to limit immune escape: two 24-amino-acid consensus peptides from the major hydrophilic region were synthesised and used to immunise laying hens. Antigen-specific IgY was extracted from egg yolks by salting-out precipitation, purified by peptide-affinity chromatography and conjugated to horseradish peroxidase by glutaraldehyde cross-linking and by sodium periodate oxidation. SDS-PAGE under reducing and non-reducing conditions confirmed the structural integrity of the purified IgY. Both chemistries yielded functional conjugates, but the periodate-oxidised conjugate gave a significantly higher signal across dilutions (Wilcoxon test, p = 0.016). In an adapted commercial sandwich ELISA applied to 10 HBsAg-positive and 10 HBsAg-negative sera, the in-house IgY-HRP conjugates produced optical density profiles that differed from the commercial biotinylated system (repeated-measures ANOVA, p < 0.0001) while separating positive from negative sera completely. Receiver-operating-characteristic analysis gave an area under the curve of 1.000 for all three detection systems, and at the Youden-derived cut-offs (OD450 0.77 for the glutaraldehyde and 0.80 for the periodate conjugate) both in-house reagents reached 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity (95% CI 72.2%-100% for each, n = 10 per group). This work establishes a low-cost, locally producible IgY-based platform for HBsAg detection, offering a scalable alternative for HBV screening in resource-limited, high-prevalence settings.

items.title: Oral and anal detection of Treponema pallidum DNA among transgender women and travestis with high-titre syphilis in Brazil: findings from the MyTTrA study.
items.abstract: Data on transgender women and travestis (TGW) concerning oral and anal detection of Treponema pallidum (TP) DNA are lacking. We aimed to estimate the prevalence of oral and anal TP DNA detection and the frequency of azithromycin resistance-associated mutations among TGW with high-titre syphilis in Brazil. We conducted a nested cross-sectional study as part of the TransOdara study among TGW in five Brazilian cities. Participants with high-titre syphilis (reactive treponemal test and VDRL titre ≥1:8) and an analysable oral or anal specimen underwent quantitative PCR targeting the tpp47 and polA genes to detect TP DNA. TP DNA-positive specimens were further analysed using nested PCR and Sanger sequencing to identify mutations associated with azithromycin resistance. Among the 249 participants with high-titre serological syphilis and analysable sample, TP DNA was detected in 25 (10.0%, 95% CI 6.6-14.5): 14 (5.6%) from the oral site only, 6 (2.4%) from the anal site only, and 5 (2.0%) from both sites. Participants in whom TP DNA was detected were younger and more frequently reported STI symptoms and anogenital ulcers during the preceding six months. The detection rate increased with VDRL titre (odds ratio 2.44, 95% CI 1.74-3.41 per doubling of titre for any oral or anal detection). Mutations associated with azithromycin resistance were observed in 76% (19/25, 95% CI 54.9-90.6) of participants in whom TP was detected. TP DNA was detected in 10% of participants with high-titre serological syphilis. Detection increased with higher VDRL titres, supporting an association between higher non-treponemal titres and mucosal TP DNA detection. These findings support continued epidemiological and molecular surveillance of syphilis and of azithromycin resistance in transgender populations. They do not support site-specific PCR screening: syphilis diagnosis remains serological, and benzathine benzylpenicillin G remains the treatment of choice. French National Agency for Research on AIDS, Viral Hepatitis, and Emerging Infectious Diseases (ANRS/MIE).

items.title: Importance of Hepatic Copper Content as a Single Diagnostic Criterion for Wilson's Disease: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Wilson's disease (WD) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the ATP7B gene, resulting in impaired copper metabolism and toxic accumulation in the liver. In pediatric patients, diagnosis may be particularly challenging due to the absence of classic manifestations. We report the case of a 4-year-old girl (16 kg) who was asymptomatic but had persistently elevated liver enzymes detected during routine evaluation from the age of one year. She had no clinical, neurological, or ophthalmologic signs suggestive of WD. Comprehensive laboratory investigations, including viral and autoimmune markers, were unremarkable. Given the persistent transaminase elevation and lack of an alternative diagnosis, a liver biopsy was performed. Histopathological examination demonstrated features consistent with chronic active hepatitis, and quantitative analysis revealed markedly elevated hepatic copper content (1605 μg/g dry weight). Subsequent whole-exome sequencing identified a homozygous ATP7B mutation, confirming the diagnosis of WD. Treatment with zinc and trientine was initiated, resulting in normalization of liver enzyme levels within 3 months. Sustained biochemical remission was maintained throughout the 1-year follow-up period. This case underscores the pivotal diagnostic role of hepatic copper quantification in children with atypical or clinically silent presentations of WD. Although serum ceruloplasmin and urinary copper excretion are widely used screening tools, they may lack sensitivity and specificity in young children. Hepatic copper measurement remains a definitive diagnostic criterion and should be strongly considered when clinical and laboratory findings are inconclusive, facilitating early diagnosis and timely initiation of therapy.

items.title: Cancer-Associated Fibroblast-Derived miR-483-5p Promotes Liver Cancer Cell Proliferation and Stemness via MOAP1 Downregulation.
items.abstract: Within the tumor microenvironment (TME), cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) play an important role in liver cancer progression through intercellular communication, including the release of small extracellular vesicles (sEVs). This study investigated the potential mechanisms underlying the effects of CAF-associated miR-483-5p on liver cancer progression. sEV-enriched preparations were isolated from CAFs transfected with a miR-483-5p mimic or an antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) and subsequently used to treat HepG2 cells. These preparations were designated as CAF-sEV-miR-483-5p-mimic and CAF-sEV-miR-483-5p-ASO, respectively. To evaluate cell proliferation and stemness, colony formation and spheroid formation assays were applied. Additionally, a subcutaneous xenograft model in nude mice was established to assess the in vivo effects of these CAF-derived sEV-enriched preparations. MiR-483-5p enhanced HepG2 cell proliferation, stemness, and migration, and higher miR-483-5p expression was associated with poorer patient prognosis. CAF-derived sEV-enriched preparations was associated with increased miR-483-5p levels in HepG2 cells, suggesting that these preparations may contribute to the regulation of miR-483-5p levels in recipient cells. The CAF-sEV-miR-483-5p mimic preparation promoted HepG2 cell proliferation and stemness while suppressing apoptosis. Luciferase reporter and reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) assays supported the direct interaction between miR-483-5p and the Modulator of apoptosis 1 (MOAP1) 3' untranslated region (3'-UTR) and showed that miR-483-5p negatively regulates MOAP1 expression. MOAP1 downregulation was associated with increased proliferation and stemness in HepG2 cells. Importantly, MOAP1 overexpression attenuated miR-483-5p-induced increases in proliferation, migration, and stemness in HepG2 cells, as well as the upregulation of Wnt1, β-catenin, Nanog, Sox2, and Oct4. Furthermore, miR-483-5p ASO reversed the effects of CAF-derived sEV-enriched preparations on miR-483-5p levels, MOAP1 expression, and HepG2 cell viability. In vivo, the CAF-sEV-miR-483-5p-mimic preparation promoted xenograft tumor growth in nude mice. Collectively, CAF-derived sEV-enriched preparations may contribute to increased miR-483-5p levels and promote the growth and stemness of liver cancer cells, potentially through miR-483-5p-mediated downregulation of MOAP1. These findings suggest that the miR-483-5p/MOAP1 regulatory axis may serve as a potential therapeutic target for liver cancer.

items.title: Causal Links Between Seborrheic Keratosis and Internal Malignancies: Evidence from Bidirectional Mendelian Randomization.
items.abstract: The association between seborrheic keratosis (SK) and internal malignancies remains controversial, with findings from observational studies often confounded by reverse causality and unmeasured confounding factors. This study aimed to investigate the causal relationship between SK and common malignancies using a bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) approach. Genetic instruments for SK and malignancies (thyroid, breast, lung, colorectal, liver, gastric, prostate, renal, and pancreatic cancer) were derived from publicly available genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics based on individuals of European ancestry. Independent single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) significantly associated with SK were used as instrumental variables. Bidirectional two-sample MR analyses were performed, primarily using the inverse-variance weighted (IVW) method, supplemented by MR-Egger, weighted median, and other robust methods. Sensitivity analyses, including Cochran's Q test, MR-Egger intercept test, and leave-one-out analysis, were conducted to assess heterogeneity, pleiotropy, and the robustness of the results. In the present study, genetically predicted SK was associated with an increased risk of breast cancer (IVW OR = 1.075, 95% CI: 1.014-1.139, P = 0.015) and colorectal cancer (IVW OR = 1.211, 95% CI: 1.069-1.371, P = 0.003). No significant causal associations were found between SK and the other seven cancers. Sensitivity analyses revealed no significant horizontal pleiotropy, and the results were robust. Reverse MR analysis did not support a causal effect of the investigated cancers on SK. This study provides genetic evidence supporting a potential causal association between SK and increased risk of breast and colorectal cancer. These findings offer new insights into the clinical significance of SK, although the underlying biological mechanisms require further elucidation.

items.title: Cryptogenic Invasive Klebsiella pneumoniae Liver Abscess Syndrome with Occult Colon Cancer: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Invasive Klebsiella pneumoniae liver abscess syndrome (IKLAS) describes K. pneumoniae liver abscess with extrahepatic metastatic infection. Although the syndrome is associated with hypervirulent K. pneumoniae (hvKP), its clinical presentation alone does not confirm hypervirulence. Occult colorectal malignancy may be identified during evaluation of apparently cryptogenic infection. A 75-year-old man presented with intermittent fever for more than 1 month and right upper abdominal pain. Imaging revealed multiple hepatic abscesses and pulmonary lesions compatible with metastatic infection. K. pneumoniae was isolated from blood and sputum cultures, supporting a clinical diagnosis of IKLAS. Hypervirulence was clinically suspected but not microbiologically confirmed because capsular serotyping and virulence-gene testing were not performed. The patient had no history of diabetes mellitus or biliary tract disease. Abdominal CT showed irregular wall thickening at the hepatic flexure, and colonoscopy with biopsy confirmed moderately to poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma. Piperacillin-tazobactam and moxifloxacin were associated with clinical improvement and radiologic regression; percutaneous drainage was deferred because of incomplete abscess liquefaction. After infection control, he underwent laparoscopic radical right hemicolectomy (pathological stage pT3N0Mx). No recurrence or distant metastasis was detected at the 9-month postoperative follow-up. This case illustrates that apparently cryptogenic IKLAS may be an initial clinical clue to occult colon cancer. Individualized colorectal evaluation may be considered, particularly in patients without common predisposing factors or with suspicious clinical or imaging findings. This single case does not establish causality or support universal screening. A 75-year-old man developed fever and abdominal pain. Doctors found liver abscesses, bacteria in his blood, and lung changes suggesting that the infection had spread. Tests identified Klebsiella pneumoniae . Doctors suspected a highly invasive strain, but they did not perform the specialized tests needed to confirm it. The man had no history of diabetes or bile duct disease. A CT scan also showed thickening of the colon wall. Doctors examined his colon with a camera and took tissue samples, which showed colon cancer. Antibiotics controlled the infection, and surgeons then removed the cancer. Follow-up tests found no cancer recurrence or spread nine months after surgery. This case suggests that an unexplained liver abscess can sometimes provide a clue to otherwise silent colon cancer. Doctors may consider further bowel assessment based on each patient’s findings and overall condition. One case cannot prove that the cancer caused the infection or that everyone with this infection needs a colonoscopy.

items.title: Outcome of magnetic resonance guided stereotactic body radiotherapy for hepatocellular carcinoma - an R-IDEAL stage IIb trial.
items.abstract: Stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is gaining increasing importance as a non-invasive, ablative treatment. However, there are still limited data on online magnetic resonance imaging-guided SBRT (MRgSBRT) for HCCs using MR linear accelerators. The aim of this study was to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and oncological outcomes of online adaptive MRgSBRT in patients with HCC. All patients who underwent liver MR-guided SBRT for HCC using fraction doses of at least 5 Gy between August 2019 and September 2024 were included. All patients were treated on a 1.5 T magnetic resonance (MR-)-Linac with MR imaging for online adaptation and motion monitoring at each fraction. Treatment-related parameters, local control (LC), overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) are reported. A total of 45 patients with 51 lesions were treated with online adaptive MRgSBRT. Median age was 72 (interquartile range, IQR 67 to 78) years. Liver-directed treatments prior to the SBRT had been applied in 53% of patients. A median of 35 (IQR of 35 to 40) Gray (Gy) was applied with a median of 5 fractions. Median follow-up was 28 months (95% confidence interval, CI: 21-35). LC at 12 and 24 months was 94% (95% CI: 86-100) and 90% (95% CI 79-100). OS after 12 and 24 months were 84% (95% CI: 73-96) and 70% (95% CI: 56-87) and PFS was 54.7% (95% CI: 41-74) and 29% (95% CI: 17%-50%). Of the 14 patients treated for bridging 8 patients (57%) proceeded to receive liver transplantation. No acute adverse events beyond CTCAE grade 2 were documented. Non-invasive, online adaptive MRgSBRT for HCC in this prospective cohort of patients proved to be well tolerated with excellent local control and is therefore a viable treatment option for patients with HCC.

items.title: Comprehensive characterisation of patients with colorectal cancer and permanently liver-limited disease.
items.abstract: Metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) shows organ-specific patterns of dissemination. Approximately 20% of patients develop disease confined to the liver throughout the course. Early recognition and characterisation of this phenotype may inform therapeutic stratification and improve outcomes. We retrospectively analysed patients with unresectable mCRC. Patients were classified by metastatic distribution into liver-limited, liver plus extrahepatic, or extrahepatic-only disease. Clinicopathological features, genomic alterations assessed by next-generation sequencing, and immune contexture based on a 12-gene signature from the primary tumour were evaluated. Among 1026 eligible patients, 20% had permanently liver-limited disease, 51% had both hepatic and extrahepatic involvement, and 29% had extrahepatic-only metastases. Liver-limited cases were enriched for synchronous presentation and nonrectal primaries, with a lower prevalence of KRAS mutations ( P = 0.013). Tumours with liver plus extrahepatic dissemination showed greater genetic alterations across multiple cancer hallmarks ( P P = 0.041). Despite similar genomic profiles, extrahepatic-only disease was associated with improved overall survival. Permanent liver-limited mCRC defines a clinically and biologically distinct subgroup characterised by synchronous onset, nonrectal primaries, and reduced KRAS mutation frequency. The immune landscape of the primary tumour was associated with metastatic organ pattern.
